fields.reasoning: The finding is confirmed in the code: stateRows() (internal/api/daemon_settings.go) copies every setting Value into daemon state, and daemon.status (ReadOnly, internal/api/daemon.go ~2057) returns those Values, served without authentication by ReadOnlyHandler (web_api.go). @{01M79Q8PX68N5R6XWD5MHV6FKJ} already says the token's value is never shown, so the intent is clear and only its coverage is incomplete. Masking per operation would leave the token in the on-disk daemon state and invite the next read-only op to leak it again; masking once where rows are built (settings rows and stateRows) closes daemon.settings, daemon.status and the state together, and needs no new scope beyond the change set's intent of a required web token. The acceptance must name daemon.status so a builder who masks only daemon.settings fails.
fields.statement: The web token's value is masked where setting rows are built, not per operation: rhiza.web.token's row carries only whether it is set, in daemon.settings, in the rows the daemon's poll copies into its state (conf.stateRows()) and so in daemon.status's Settings, and in every read-only operation served unauthenticated at GET /api/<op>. The daemon's web handler reads the token itself from the setting, never from state or a response. @{01M79Q8PX68N5R6XWD5MHV6FKJ}'s acceptance gains a check that daemon.status and an unauthenticated GET /api/daemon.status through WebProjectHandler do not return the token's value.
